Definition: from G4535; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite:--move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.
BiblicalUsage: The word saleúō means to waver, that is agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite. In 2 Thessalonians 2:2, we read, "…soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither…"; in Acts 2:25, "…David speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord…". You hear it again in Hebrews 12:26 — "…now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more…" — and in Luke 6:38, "…you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that saleúō is no accident in the text, and it names something real, and God does not use empty words. And I hold that saleúō is as true now as when it was first written, because God does not change.
